0.0.n: This sets the time without needing a particle.

0.3.n: 黒い床 refers to the surface he was afraid to step onto.

0.4.n: に marks the destination of 行く.

0.5.n: The plain form comes before こと to make the action into a noun-like phrase.

0.6.n: こと turns 行く into something that can be the object of fear.

0.7.n: を marks 行くこと as what he feared; English uses afraid of instead.

0.8.n: 非常 combines with に to describe how strongly he felt fear.

0.9.n: に makes 非常 modify 恐れていた rather than a noun.

0.10.n: 恐れる becomes 恐れていた through ていた, describing an ongoing state of fear in the past.

1.0.n: なぜ asks for a reason and sounds more formal than どうして.

1.1.n: This is the first part of だろう, which expresses wondering here rather than certainty.

1.2.n: う completes だろう; it is not a separate word here.

0.lit: First day, black floor onto going very much feared.
0.tip: 行くこと turns going into the thing he feared; the Japanese leaves he unstated.

1.tip: Read だろ and う together as だろう, expressing a question the speaker wonders about.
